cards.explanation: The answer is the throne of Satan. Jesus says, "I know where you live, where the throne of Satan sits…" (Revelation 2:13). He doesn't pretend the address is easy. And notice He says it before He says one word about what they did right.

The answer is True! Jesus says, "…yet you hold fast to My name. You did not deny your faith in Me…" (Revelation 2:13). Look at that "yet," friends. The address is rough, and they held on anyway. Jesus saw it and said so out loud.
The answer is False. Jesus says, "…some of you hold to the teaching of Balaam…" (Revelation 2:14). Some, not all. That one little word keeps us from painting the whole church with one brush.

The answer is the Nicolaitans. Jesus says, "In the same way, some of you also hold to the teaching of the Nicolaitans." (Revelation 2:15). Right after Balaam, here's a second teaching. The text doesn't say more about them in this passage, so I won't make anything up.
The word is repent. Jesus says, "Therefore repent!" (Revelation 2:16). It's short and clear, and it's a call to turn. He says it right after naming what's wrong, so they know exactly what He means.

The answer is True. Jesus says, "Otherwise I will come to you shortly and wage war against them with the sword of My mouth." (Revelation 2:16). He says "them," and the text doesn't spell out who that is, so I'll leave it there. And remember who opened this letter, the One with the sharp, double-edged sword (Revelation 2:12).

The answer is a new name. Jesus says, "I will also give him a white stone inscribed with a new name, known only to the one who receives it." (Revelation 2:17). A stone with a new name on it, and only the one who gets it knows that name. That's a gift made for one person.
The answer is False. Jesus says the new name is "…known only to the one who receives it." (Revelation 2:17). So the rest of the church doesn't know it. Only the one who gets the stone does.
The answer is greater than their first. Jesus says, "…your latest deeds are greater than your first." (Revelation 2:19). That's a church still growing, friends, and He notices.

The answer is True. Jesus says, "You tolerate that woman Jezebel, who calls herself a prophetess." (Revelation 2:20). He praised their deeds first, and now He names what He has against them. Both things are in the same letter.

The answer is that she is unwilling. Jesus says, "Even though I have given her time to repent of her immorality, she is unwilling." (Revelation 2:21). Time was given. She didn't take it. That's what the text says, and I won't add a reason it doesn't give.

The answer is great tribulation unless they repent. Jesus says, "…those who commit adultery with her will suffer great tribulation unless they repent of her deeds." (Revelation 2:22). Look at that "unless." The door to repent is still open for them. This is a heavy part, friends.

The answer is that He searches minds and hearts. Jesus says, "…all the churches will know that I am the One who searches minds and hearts…" (Revelation 2:23). He sees what's inside, not just what's on the outside. That's a comfort for anyone trying to be honest with Him.

The answer is False. Jesus says to the rest of Thyatira, "I will place no further burden upon you" (Revelation 2:24). The faithful ones aren't getting a pile of new rules. That's a kind thing to hear after all those heavy lines.

The word is comes. Jesus says, "…than to hold fast to what you have until I come." (Revelation 2:25). It's what He told them to hold onto, until He comes. That's why I keep my ovens warm, friends. I just never guess when.
The answer is False. Jesus promises "…authority over the nations." (Revelation 2:26). That's way bigger than one church. It goes to the one who overcomes and continues in His work until the end.

The answer is from His Father. Jesus says, "…just as I have received authority from My Father." (Revelation 2:27). Whatever the overcomer gets, it's tied to what Jesus Himself received from the Father. It's a gift, not something grabbed.
